items.title: Physics of Language Models: Part 4.2, Canon Layers at Scale where Synthetic Pretraining Resonates in Reality
items.description:
arXiv:2611.24963v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Do standard benchmarks see the architectural differences that matter? We study it with 64 from-scratch pretraining runs of Transformers and three linear-model families at 1.3-8B parameters on 1-2T Nemotron-CC tokens, at a cost of roughly 100k USD per
items.summary: Researchers conducted 64 new pretraining experiments with different architectural designs to assess their impact on standard language model benchmarks, spending about 100k USD each. This study aims to highlight architectural differences that current benchmarks might not effectively capture, emphasizing the need for more nuanced evaluation methods in large-scale language models.
items.summary_detailed: Researchers conducted extensive experiments using 64 custom Transformer models with varying parameter sizes to explore the impact of architectural differences in large language models. The study involved running these models on massive datasets containing up to 2 trillion tokens and found that standard benchmarks may not fully capture the nuances of model architecture. This research has broader implications for how future language models are designed and evaluated, potentially leading to more effective and efficient training methods.
items.summary_bullets:
• Study involves 64 from-scratch pretraining runs of Transformers and linear models.
• Experiments use 1.3-8 billion parameters across three model families.
• Benchmarks analyzed include those with 1-2 trillion Nemotron-CC tokens.
• Each run costs approximately 100,000 USD.
